questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good weather, good school, beautiful surroundings, English speaking.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too easy. I had a lot of trouble with reagards to course enrolment.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not very much. I found it quite difficult to find out who to turn to with respect to academia. There was a lot of introduction, but it seemed more suited for transfer students rather than exchange student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You got assigned a place and could accept or not. I did not get a spot in any of the dorms I applied for.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were available but I had my own kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus is way too expensive. Apply for I-House or the coops.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In America everything is quite difficult, a lot of paperwork and so on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were phone numbers you could call. But the time difference makes it difficult.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not too succesfull. As mentioned above it was very difficult. As an exchange student, you have the lowest priority. Avoid mathematical classes in the US, I believe the level is lower than in Europe. Do a lot of computer science instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a lot of patience, and find some of the other people that are going and do it together. Write down all the deadlines and make sure to do what is asked before them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I believe the level of the mathematical classes at Berkeley, is lower than in Europe. Computer science classes on the other hand were excellent.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: During the semester there were a lot of deadlines and assignments to hand in. There were midterms and a lot of your grade is determined beforehand. You are being forced to do the work during the semester instead of in the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CS61A ( excellent course), Linear Models (stat151A), Machine Learning (stat154), and introduction to advanced programming in R.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do a lot of computer science. CS61a was incredible, and I believe CS61B and C would be too. If you are a student of mathematics and statistics in Europe then stay away from these fields at Berkeley.,

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of trips, which can be quite expensive (spring break). Also life is quite expensive. Food and stuff is more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive. Live in a coop! Food is included and it is way cheaper than anything else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very big variety of all kinds of activities. This was very nice to experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved to play tennis (for free!!), going on trips and hikes, climbing, going to different classes in RSF, the chess club, free Wednesday cinema, going for runs at fire trails. All kinds of stuff!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lake Tahoe, Yosemite, Point Reyes, San Fran and all the other stuff. So much to do! Go to sports games.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time. Especially the first few weeks are tough. Living with a roommate is weird too.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and approach people. It was quite easy befriending people at Berkeley. And say yes, all the time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to be very careful not to offend. Especially politically there is a right and a wrong. And the culture is different, as a European you will be surprised. But it was not challenging. Maybe the consumerism.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The college culture. There is so much life and so many things happening at college.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is a lot of work, but if you have the energy and the will to go it is definitely worth it. And do computer science and not statistics ;)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to coops, and do computer science.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Academia.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
